I found the cause of the 500, but I haven't fixed it. `article.service.ts` is unchanged. The Edit tool isn't enabled in this session, and the PowerShell tool rejected each way I tried to write the file. I stopped there rather than keep trying workarounds.

**Cause:** `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` calls `ArticleService.favorite()`. That method loads the user with `findOne(id)`, but `UserEntity.favorites` is a plain `@ManyToMany` that isn't loaded automatically. So `user.favorites` is `undefined`, and `.findIndex` at `article.service.ts:135` throws a `TypeError`, which becomes the 500. `LESSONS.md` records the same bug.

**Fix:** change line 133 of `src/article/article.service.ts`, the same way `create()` already loads `articles`:

```ts
// before
const user = await this.userRepository.findOne(id);
// after
const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id }, relations: ['favorites'] });
```

Nothing is tested. There's no `node_modules` in `fixture/` and no test covers this route.

**Other bugs I found but did not touch** (you asked only about favorite):

| Item | What's wrong | Needed now? |
|---|---|---|
| `unFavorite()` (line 149) | Same missing relation, so `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` also returns 500. It's the same one-line fix. | Probably yes |
| `findAll()` `?favorited=` (lines 44–46) | Same missing relation. It also compares article ids against `authorId`, so even once it loads the result is wrong. | Separate fix |
| `favorite()` with an unknown slug | `article` is `undefined`, so you get a 500 instead of a 404. | No |

**Your call:** enable the Edit tool, or allow shell writes to `src/`, and I'll apply the fix. Or apply the one-line change yourself. Say whether to include `unFavorite()` in the same change.
